newsitem.title: YEMEN: U.N. allocates $200 million for Yemen projects.
newsitem.headline: U.N. allocates $200 million for Yemen projects.

text.p: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has allocated $200 million to help launch projects in Yemen over the next five years, a UNDP official said on Sunday.

"The amount will be used for different projects," Saad al-Farargi, director of the UNDP's regional bureau for Arab states, told a news conference on the sidelines of a symposium on growth in the Arab world held in Sanaa.
Yemen, the Arab world's poorest state with per capita income of $280 a year, is trying to lure foreign investment and aid to support its ailing economy.
In 1995 Yemen, which relies on oil for 75 percent of income, began an economic reform package with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
